text: Connect an MCP client through an authentication workflow, with permission for all graphs or a selection
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: for connecting MCPs, build an authenticate workflow with permission: all graphs, or just a selection of graphs (repos).

This is how an agent acts on a server: through a person's account, limited to the graphs that person chose. Felix 2026-11-11: non-human agents get a user identity too and are shown on the ideas they work on while they work.

Today: the UI has "Copy MCP link", which carries the account's token in the address (?token=) or as a bearer header (mcp/src/sse.ts); the token has all rights of the account, on the one project the server hosts. af701cd6 had planned a login page opened by the MCP client, which was not built.

Not designed: whether the agent appears under the person's name or under a name of its own tied to that person.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Most people never find the MCP entry in the account menu; asked at the moment they open a space, many connect an assistant and then work with it in the space.

status.comment: Built 2026-11-13 (50e24bd6, e2eaf826). Two ways. In the UI, "MCP" in the account corner: choose all graphs or a selection, get a link shown once, list and revoke connected clients. Or the client logs in by itself at <host>/mcp/login/sse (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and client registration on the MCP SDK's router, needs server.json publicUrl): it opens the server's page, the person chooses graphs and approves. Either way the token is the account on the chosen graphs and nobody elsewhere. A graph's own address (<host>/g/<slug>/mcp/sse) serves a session whose tools need no projectPath. Evidence: backend auth/auth.test.ts (limited token), auth/mcp-clients.test.ts; mcp oauth.test.ts runs the whole login with the SDK's own client code (discovery, registration, authorization page, PKCE, token, session). Not tried: a real MCP client such as Claude Code against a running server. Still undecided: the agent appears under the person's name; a name of its own was not designed.
